findings.title: verify() never checks session expiry
findings.description: verify() loops over sessions and returns any matching token regardless of expiresAt, so expired sessions remain valid indefinitely. The documented contract says an expired token resolves to undefined.

findings.title: requireAdmin rejects the admin role
findings.description: `allowed.indexOf(session.role)` returns 0 for "admin", and 0 is falsy, so `if` is false and admins are rejected while role "owner" (index 1) passes. The intended membership test is never true for "admin".

findings.title: bearerToken dereferences undefined header
findings.description: With no Authorization header, `header!.split` throws an unhandled TypeError instead of a controlled 401. Using non-null assertions on possibly-undefined input crashes the request path.

findings.title: parseLifetimeHours can return NaN
findings.description: parseInt of a non-numeric string yields NaN, which propagates into TTL arithmetic and produces an invalid expiry. No validation or fallback.

findings.title: delete() leaves the TTL timer running
findings.description: The scheduled setTimeout is never cleared, so an expired-timer callback can later delete a freshly inserted entry with the same code, and timers accumulate. Resource leak and stale deletion.

findings.title: set() does not clear a pre-existing timer on overwrite
findings.description: Re-caching a code leaves the old timer armed; combined with the leak in delete(), timers accumulate and can evict/expire the new entry prematurely. Also eviction of the victim leaves its timer armed.

findings.title: LRU eviction is not actually LRU
findings.description: get() updates entry.used but never updates Map insertion order, and set() evicts `this.entries.keys().next()` (insertion order). Under load the cache evicts by insertion order, not least-recently used, contradicting the contract.

findings.title: keys() always returns an empty array
findings.description: Iterating a Map with `for (const key in this.entries)` enumerates own enumerable string properties, which a Map has none of, so the admin view always sees an empty cache.

findings.title: utilization() is 0 for any partially full cache
findings.description: Math.floor(size / limit) is 0 whenever size < limit, so the dashboard reports 0% until the cache is completely full. Multiplier is applied after flooring.

findings.title: peek() ignores expiry
findings.description: peek() returns true for entries that have expired but not yet been swept, so warm()/callers treat a stale entry as present and skip refreshing it.

findings.title: loadConfig mutates the shared DEFAULT_CONFIG
findings.description: `const cfg = DEFAULT_CONFIG` aliases the exported default object, so environment-driven values permanently leak into DEFAULT_CONFIG across calls/tests and the original defaults are lost.

findings.title: Bad LINKD_TIMEOUT_MS still overwrites config
findings.description: When `isNaN(ms)` is true the code logs and then unconditionally sets `cfg.timeoutMs = ms`, storing NaN; validation later treats NaN comparisons as false-ish but the running timeout is invalid.

findings.title: LINKD_CACHE_TTL_MS double-converted to milliseconds
findings.description: The field is documented as milliseconds, but the value is multiplied by 1000, turning 300000ms into ~3.5 days. Inconsistent with LINKD_TIMEOUT_MS, which is used as-is.

findings.title: LINKD_FETCH_LIMIT is parsed but never applied
findings.description: The parsed limit is discarded (`void limit`), so cfg.fetchLimit always stays at the default 32 regardless of configuration.

findings.title: validate() always returns true
findings.description: Despite collecting problems, it returns true unconditionally, so bad configs pass startup validation as documented by the function.

findings.title: loadFile silently stores NaN for bad cache_size
findings.description: parseInt of a non-numeric value is assigned without finiteness check, corrupting cacheSize.

findings.title: report() export/read name mismatch when name is empty
findings.description: exportCsv defaults an empty name to "links" but readReport builds the path from the empty name, producing ".csv"/different file. The download then reads the wrong (possibly nonexistent) file.

findings.title: parseReport emits a trailing empty row
findings.description: Splitting on "\n" produces a final empty string, which becomes a row with undefined-ish cells. Consumers get one bogus row.

findings.title: resolve() treats unexpired links as expired
findings.description: The condition `Date.now() < link.expiresAt` triggers deletion and returns undefined for links that are still valid, while expired links proceed to increment hits and return target. This inverts the expiry semantics and breaks every redirect.

findings.title: create() corrupts quota when owner is new
findings.description: `this.quota[owner]! + 1` is NaN when the owner has no prior entry, because `undefined + 1` is NaN. Quota tracking is broken for first-time owners.

findings.title: delete() does not return the owner's quota slot
findings.description: Despite the documented contract, quota is never decremented, so deleted links permanently consume an owner's quota.

findings.title: rename() validates the source code twice and never validates target
findings.description: `validateCode(from)` is called twice while `to` is unchecked, so invalid target codes can be introduced.

findings.title: page() slices one past the end
findings.description: When offset+size exceeds length, end is set to `all.length + 1`, over-slicing by one (clamped by Array.prototype.slice but incorrect intent and relies on clamping).

findings.title: successRate() multiplies by 100 after flooring
findings.description: `Math.floor(used / size) * 100` is 0 unless every link has hits, so the dashboard reports 0% for any partial usage.

findings.title: top() sorts ascending instead of descending
findings.description: The comparator returns positive when a.hits > b.hits, yielding ascending order, then slices the first n — returning the least-followed links rather than the most-followed.

findings.title: byOwner() uses substring match instead of exact equality
findings.description: `l.owner.includes(owner)` matches owners whose name contains the string, violating the documented "exactly this owner" filtering and leaking other owners' links.

findings.title: extend() revives already-expired links
findings.description: The documented contract says an expired link stays expired, but extend unconditionally sets a new expiresAt, bringing dead codes back to life.

findings.title: quotas() exposes the internal mutable map
findings.description: Returning `this.quota` directly lets callers mutate store state, violating the documented snapshot semantics.

findings.title: importAll() is not atomic and skips quota updates
findings.description: Links are inserted one at a time with no rollback on later failure, and quotas are never incremented, so a failed batch partially mutates the store and quota bookkeeping drifts.

findings.title: prune() returns size instead of removed count
findings.description: The documented return value is the number removed, but it returns `this.links.size`. Callers relying on the count are misinformed.

findings.title: expiresAt() can crash on unknown code
findings.description: The non-null assertion `this.links.get(code)!.expiresAt` throws when the code is absent, instead of returning a defined sentinel.

findings.title: warmCache resolves before probes finish and drops rejections
findings.description: Using `pairs.forEach(async ...)` fires unawaited promises; `warmCache` resolves immediately and any probe rejection becomes an unhandled rejection. Contradicts "resolves once every probe has finished."

findings.title: flushAudit does not await write() or retry
findings.description: The write promise is discarded, so failures are swallowed and the documented retry-until-success never happens.

findings.title: countForOwner returns NaN for unknown owner
findings.description: `quotas[owner] + 0` is NaN when the owner has no entry.

findings.title: handle() dereferences bearerToken result that may be undefined
findings.description: With no Authorization header, bearerToken throws, so the 401 path is unreachable and the request crashes instead.

findings.title: deleteLink ignores ownership and never updates quota
findings.description: It calls store.delete(code) without checking the authenticated session's owner, despite the comment that only the creator may delete; also silently no-ops quota via store.

findings.title: stats() divides by zero when store is empty
findings.description: `store.totalHits() / store.size()` yields NaN (and Infinity) when there are no links, corrupting the stats response.

findings.title: createLink treats ttl=0 as unset
findings.description: `payload.ttl ?` is falsy for "0", so an explicitly requested zero TTL falls back to the 30-day default.

findings.title: createLink does not validate parsed TTL
findings.description: parseInt of a non-numeric ttl yields NaN, producing NaN expiresAt; negative/zero values are not bounds-checked.

findings.title: warmCache resolves before its probes finish
findings.description: The body is `pairs.forEach(async ...)` with no await at the top level, so `warmCache`'s returned promise resolves as soon as the synchronous forEach returns, well before `probe`/`cache.set` complete. Callers that `await warmCache` therefore run against a cache that is not actually warm, and the overlapping in-flight probes can interleave their `cache.set` writes with request handling, mutating shared cache state (and accumulating expiry timers) concurrently with readers. Scenario: handler awaits warmCache then reads a code that was supposed to be primed -> miss, while probes from the warm run are still landing afterward.

findings.title: Expired-entry timers are never cleared and can delete a fresh entry
findings.description: `set` schedules `setTimeout(() => this.delete(code), ttlMs)` and stores the handle in `timers`, but `delete` never calls `clearTimeout`, and `set` never cancels a prior handle for the same code. Any early eviction, manual delete, or replacement leaves a stale timer that later fires and deletes whatever (possibly freshly cached) entry currently occupies `code`. Scenario: set(code,A); delete(code); set(code,B, fresh TTL); the first timer fires after the original TTL and removes B even though B is still live. With overlapping warm runs this becomes a data-loss race on the shared cache.

findings.title: flushAudit fires write without awaiting or retrying
findings.description: Documented as 'retried until it succeeds', but it just calls `write()` and discards the returned promise. If `write` is async and rejects, the rejection is unhandled and the audit line is silently lost; there is no ordering/cancellation guarantee between concurrent flush calls on the same audit resource. Scenario: two concurrent callers invoke flushAudit with writes to the same file; the first's floating promise can resolve after the second's has started, producing interleaved/corrupt appends with no error surfaced.

findings.title: Janitor interval handle is discarded, so it can never be stopped
findings.description: `startJanitor` returns a stopper but the return value is ignored, so the `setInterval` lives for the whole process and is never cleared. Each start (including repeated starts in tests or hot reload) leaks another interval that keeps mutating the shared store on a timer, in parallel with request handling. Scenario: reload/re-init path calls startJanitor twice -> two sweepers deleting expired links concurrently with requests; harmless per event loop today, but unbounded growth and no graceful shutdown.

findings.title: Hardcoded fallback secret
findings.description: When LINKD_SECRET is unset, the service falls back to the well-known constant 'dev-secret-do-not-use'. Any deployment that forgets to set the env var is then protected by a publicly known secret recoverable from source, and getSecret() exposes it to callers.

findings.title: Session tokens minted with Math.random
findings.description: Tokens are built from Math.random() and Date.now(), both predictable and not cryptographically secure. An attacker who can observe timing or guess seeds can forge a session token and impersonate owners/admins.

findings.title: Session token written to logs
findings.description: issue() logs the full bearer token. Anyone with log access (operators, aggregators, error trackers) can replay it until expiry, bypassing authentication.

findings.title: requireAdmin authorization logic is inverted/broken
findings.description: allowed.indexOf(session.role) is used in a boolean context. indexOf returns 0 for 'admin', which is falsy, so admins are rejected, while 'owner' (index 1) is truthy and accepted. This mis-grants admin capabilities to owner-role sessions and denies real admins.

findings.title: Password hashing uses fast unsalted SHA-256
findings.description: hashPassword is a single SHA-256 pass with no salt. Stored digests are vulnerable to rainbow tables and fast offline cracking; equal passwords produce identical hashes, enabling account correlation.

findings.title: bearerToken dereferences possibly-undefined header
findings.description: header! and parts[1]! assert presence. A request with no Authorization header throws inside handle() before the 401 path, causing an unhandled exception/500 (or process crash) and enabling cheap denial of service.

findings.title: secretEquals is not constant-time despite its contract
findings.description: The function is documented as not leaking how much matched but uses `===`, a short-circuiting comparison. Timing differences can reveal the secret byte-by-byte.

findings.title: Permissive CORS combined with credentials
findings.description: Responses send Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * together with Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true. This configuration is rejected by browsers and signals an unsafe cross-origin policy; if tightened naively later it could expose authenticated endpoints to any origin.

findings.title: Unknown token echoed in 401 response
findings.description: The 401 body includes the presented token. This leaks credentials into browser histories, proxies, and access logs and aids token fixation/replay attempts.

findings.title: Unvalidated JSON.parse can throw uncaught
findings.description: createLink calls JSON.parse(req.body) outside any try. Malformed bodies throw synchronously inside handle(), producing 500s (and potential process crashes) rather than a 400, enabling cheap denial of service.

findings.title: Link owner taken from request body instead of session
findings.description: createLink uses payload.owner for ownership. Any authenticated user can create links attributed to another owner, consuming/bypassing that owner's quota and polluting their data (impersonation).

findings.title: deleteLink lacks ownership check
findings.description: delete() is invoked with only the code; the session is never consulted. Any authenticated user can delete any other user's link by guessing/knowing its code (IDOR).

findings.title: Open redirect via /out?next=
findings.description: The next parameter is used verbatim as the Location. Attackers can send victims a trusted-domain link that redirects to a phishing site, abusing the service's reputation.

findings.title: Admin endpoint gated by spoofable header
findings.description: adminQuotas checks req.headers['x-admin'] === 'true' instead of the authenticated session's role. Any client sets the header and reads all owners' quota data, a privilege escalation.

findings.title: Path traversal in report name
findings.description: name is interpolated into a filesystem path both in exportCsv and readReport with no containment check. A value like '../../etc/passwd' can read or overwrite arbitrary files under the service account.

findings.title: exportCsv does not confine name to dir
findings.description: join(dir, `${reportName}.csv`) permits traversal through '../' segments in name, enabling arbitrary file write within the process's permissions. Coupled with readReport, this is full read/write path traversal.

findings.title: archiveAll writes owner-controlled filenames
findings.description: Owner keys are used directly as filenames (`${owner}.csv`). A malicious/crafted owner containing '../' writes files outside dir, allowing path traversal during archive export.

findings.title: Predictable shared temp file for snapshot
findings.description: writeSnapshot always uses /tmp/linkd-snapshot.json. Concurrent invocations and local users can race or plant content there (TOCTOU), corrupting the snapshot or reading secrets.

findings.title: Export files created with default world-readable mode
findings.description: writeFileSync uses default mode 0666 (umask). Despite the comment promising service-user-only access, reports and snapshots are readable by any local account.

findings.title: byOwner uses substring match
findings.description: Filtering with l.owner.includes(owner) returns links whose owner merely contains the query, leaking other users' links in owner-scoped views.

findings.title: Short codes generated from Math.random
findings.description: newCode uses Math.random, which is not cryptographically secure. Codes are short (8 chars) and partially predictable, easing brute-force enumeration of links and potential access to private targets.

findings.title: validate() always returns true
findings.description: Configuration validation collects problems but unconditionally returns true, so invalid values (port out of range, non-positive timeout, negative cache size) are accepted at startup and surface later as runtime failures or resource exhaustion.
